articles.title: Comet C/2022 E3 (ZTF)
articles.summary: The article introduces Comet C/2022 E3 (ZTF) as the first bright comet of 2023, expected to become visible to the naked eye with a maximum magnitude of 4.6 in early February. Unique for its proximity to Polaris in January, it will offer long observation periods for sky-watchers and astrophotographers. Telescope observation is possible in December in the constellation Corona Borealis.

articles.title: SJAA is an Annual Supporter of the International Dark-Sky Association!
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) is an annual supporter of the International Dark-Sky Association (IDA), an organization dedicated to protecting the night sky from light pollution. The article highlights IDA's broad relevance to various fields beyond astronomy and details SJAA's increased financial contribution and collaborative efforts, such as supporting Pinnacles National Park's dark sky designation. It underscores the importance of supporting IDA's work and building public awareness through outreach.

articles.title: Congrats Karen Bieber!
articles.summary: Karen Bieber, a member of SJAA, won the Panstarrs Comet Image Contest for her stunning astrophotograph of K2 PanSTARRS comet passing by the M10 Globular Cluster. Despite considering herself a beginner in astrophotography, having only started in April 2021, her well-timed shot taken on July 14, 2022, earned her the recognition, which was first published in the Losmandy Press Newsletter. The article also details the specific imaging equipment and software she utilized for this award-winning photo.

articles.title: Pinnacles Star Party Report
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) successfully restarted its popular public star parties at Pinnacles National Park after a pandemic-induced hiatus. Several events from April to September attracted hundreds of guests and numerous astronomers, offering impressive views of celestial objects and dark sky education. These highly praised gatherings provided memorable cosmic experiences for visitors and excellent observing opportunities for participants, with a planned October event canceled due to weather.

articles.title: SJAA Member Astrophoto Gallery
articles.summary: This document features a gallery of astrophotography submitted by members of the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA). Each entry details the photographer, celestial subject (e.g., Iris Nebula, Veil Nebula, Milky Way), date (September 24, 2022), primary location (Pinnacles National Park area), and the specific imaging equipment and software utilized for their capture.

articles.title: Observing Algol an eclipsing binary
articles.summary: The article describes Algol, an eclipsing binary star in the constellation Perseus, known for its periodic changes in brightness. This occurs when a cooler, dimmer companion star passes in front of the hotter primary star. Observers can detect these changes without a telescope by comparing Algol's brightness to nearby stars like ε Persei and γ Andromedae, and can find predicted times for its dimming (minima) online to observe the rapid reduction in light.

articles.title: Hubble Views a Billowing Cosmic Cloud
articles.summary: The NASA/ESA Hubble Space Telescope has captured an image of CB 130-3, a dense core of gas and dust located in the constellation Serpens. This object is a stellar nursery, harboring a fledgling star deep within its structure. Astronomers used Hubble's Wide Field Camera 3 to study the environment of this developing star, measuring the cloud's density and the reddening effect on background stars to understand its inner composition and the star formation process.

articles.title: Kid Spot
articles.summary: This "Kid Spot" article features astronomy-themed jokes and an engaging scavenger hunt designed for observing the Moon's surface. It provides descriptions of various lunar features like craters, maria, rilles, and domes, encouraging readers to use optical aids for observation. The article also includes a brief history of the Moon's formation and geological evolution.

articles.title: From the Board of Directors
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) has resumed in-person activities like star parties following the lifting of mask mandates, while closely monitoring the COVID-19 situation. The article announces upcoming elections for board members and officers in February and March 2023, and details discussions from recent board meetings regarding volunteer roles, the 2023 calendar, minors policy, and lifetime membership. SJAA also issues a call for volunteers to help further its mission.

articles.title: SJAA Programs & Resources
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) provides a wide array of programs and resources for its members and the community, focusing on education, equipment access, and shared astronomical experiences. These offerings include a library, telescope repair services, solar and night sky observing sessions, beginner-friendly Quick STARt and Intro to the Night Sky programs, an equipment loaner program, and specialized Astro Imaging groups and workshops, alongside school outreach star parties.
